task1_split3_outgroup_merged_code.statement: If out-group pull requests face a higher acceptance bar, out-group merged code should show an equal or lower fix-forward rate and an equal or lower revert rate than in-group merged code.
task1_split3_outgroup_merged_code.opposite_reading: If out-group merged code fails more often, the quality explanation gains support.

task3_core_residual.statement: The bitcoin/bitcoin residual of shared health, after log total pull requests, log distinct active contributors per year, and years of history, is negative.

task4_effect_versus_size_adjusted_residu.statement: Spearman correlation of each effect estimate with the size-adjusted health residual, not the raw health index.

E2_reciprocity_excess.reason: A larger reciprocity excess is the pathology, so the estimate should be higher where the residual is worse.

E3_log_hours_to_next_same_direction_top5.reason: The signed effect is negative when a top-5 first review is followed sooner. A healthier residual should move that gap toward zero.

E5_log_participants_on_log_days.reason: A larger slowdown per participant is the pathology, so the estimate should be higher where the residual is worse.

E7_first_tone_on_merge_given_later_tone.reason: A stronger first-tone association with merge is the pathology, so the estimate should be higher where the residual is worse.

E12_ingroup_on_no_peer_response.reason: The signed effect is negative when in-group authors are unanswered less often. A healthier residual should move that gap toward zero.
